title: Yup
description: Schema builder for value parsing and validation.

data.text: Yup lets you define schemas for parsing and validating values at runtime.

data.title: Yup schema

data.text: Yup describes a schema as a chain: `Yup.object({...})`, with `.required()`, `.min()`, `.email()`, `.oneOf()`. Casting and validation happen together, and the schema is reusable in a form or on the server. It is the schema library that Formik integrates with directly.

data.title: A signup schema

data.text: `.when()` makes a field depend on another, which is how a "state is required only for certain countries" rule is written. `.test()` adds an arbitrary check. Conditionals and cross-field rules are where a declarative schema earns its keep, because the logic lives next to the shape it describes.

data.title: Conditional required fields
Yup vs Zod
data.text: Yup predates Zod and is battle-tested in the Formik ecosystem; Zod is TypeScript-first and infers types automatically with `z.infer`. If your project is TypeScript, Zod removes the duplicate type definition; if it is deeply invested in Formik and JavaScript, Yup is the natural fit. Name that, rather than declaring a winner.
